Subject: Re: (urgent) streaming responses hang — chunked transfer / WS timeouts

Hi Connor / Marissa,

We started seeing a pattern around 07:50 PST where our checkout-recommendation stream (WebSocket) begins returning partial payloads and then stalls for ~30-60s before the client finally times out. This is causing failed recommendations during peak traffic and elevated error rates (5-7% across traffic, usually <0.2%). Latency to first chunk also spiked from ~120ms to >1.2s for many requests.

We collected app-side traces and a PCAP — attaching a short capture and logs. The problem looks correlated with backend 503s from your edge and intermittent chunked transfer resets (RST/FIN seen). Can you triage immediately? This is impacting our checkout conversion and procurement wants daily updates.

We need an ETA for mitigation and whether there's a recommended immediate fallback (e.g., switch to polling or reduce streaming keepalive). Happy to join a call.

Thanks,
Sarah Jensen

On Fri, Apr 9, 2027 at 8:25 AM connor_obrien@redwood.com wrote:
> Sarah — thanks for the quick heads-up and for the capture. We've alerted engineering and Marissa is looking at the traces now.

Sarah / team — quick triage update from runtime:

- Observed pattern: short bursts of significantly increased tail latency on the streaming worker pool coincident with many inflight sessions renewing large KV caches (~10-15% of requests spike cache refresh). During those bursts, our edge layer has been cutting connections earlier (~30s) due to chunked-transfer keepalive resets from overloaded workers. This lines up with the RST/FINs you captured.
- Root candidates: a) cache heavy requests + large sequence lengths causing worker CPU serialization, b) a small subset of model variants with an inefficient attention kernel at these sequence lengths.

Immediate mitigation (we can do within 20–40 minutes):
1) Edge config: reduce streaming keepalive timeout from 90s -> 20s and enable aggressive chunk-flush to avoid long-lived idle TCP windows (temporary).
2) Suggest client's fallback: short-polling to recommendations for 30 minutes while we roll a worker restart and pin traffic away from the affected model variant.

Marissa attaching a small diagnostic bundle with the relevant runtime traces and a recommended edge flag: attach: pcaps + runtime_trace_excerpt.txt

We'll also pin Acme traffic to a separate worker pool to reduce multi-tenant interference; that requires a low-risk config rollout and will be completed within the hour after approval.

—Marissa
